P1.evidence: No setter notes or application read back. Frame was three-part, not four: 'I just want to get a quick picture of where you're actually at right now... what have you tried, and where you're trying to get to' — no 'what you need' element and no explicit 'does that work?' agreement request, though the prospect did answer 'Cool. Yeah, sounds good.' The opener also led with the pitch ('happy to walk you through the whole program... the investment side') before discovery.

P2.evidence: Height and weight were asked directly ('You weigh 64?' / 'And how tall are you?') but age was volunteered unprompted ('I'm 50'), so P2a is only partial. Occupation was never asked — the prospect mentioned being an event director in passing. Health and injury history surfaced because the prospect raised the hip replacements; the rep's only probe was 'When did you do that surgery, the hip?' — no systematic screen for conditions or limitations. Training week asked directly: 'And how many times a week do you work out?' Diet asked directly: 'do you follow any kind of diet, or like, you eat all?' Results from current training, sleep and daily energy were never asked at all.

P3.evidence: P3b ran cleanly: 'What would be the like one thing that you want to work on?' — which produced mobility. No aesthetics/function question and no 'something you want to do but can't'. The bridge to underlying drive was a weaker variant — 'Do you feel like there's anything, like, left on the table that could be more? Like, what's the next level for you look like?' — and the rep did not follow the answer down. The one impact move was the rep supplying the motive himself rather than eliciting it: 'show your sons who's the man over here still, yeah? That would be your main driver?' The prospect had already handed over deep material unprompted — the separation, 'reconnecting to who I was', training as 'a coping mechanism, a positive one' — and the rep did not pick any of it up.

P4.evidence: Never run. The prospect volunteered his failed attempts unprompted — 'I tried all these online programs, like fix your hips without surgery and stuff like that, and it didn't work' and the too-basic free guide — but the rep asked none of the past-attempts or root-cause questions. The prospect then argued the opposite of the script's root-cause frame in the rep's face ('really it all works... what it takes is, it's consistency, you have to show up consistently') and the rep did not engage it.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The two-year question, the 'willing to settle for that' test, the 'why not' and the line in the sand were all absent. The rep instead validated the status quo — 'From what I'm hearing, it's not something that's wrong right now, you're just basically trying to, I don't know, optimize a little bit better' — which removed any cost of inaction before the offer was made.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The rep went from a summary straight into 'let me just show you how we actually work' and then to price, without ever asking whether the prospect believed he could get there with the right structure or whether anything would stop him going all in. Hesitation surfaced immediately after the number and there was no return to Phase 5, because Phase 5 had never been run.

P11.evidence: The phase was never reachable. The rep stated the mechanics conditionally — 'Like, we settled the payments, I get you on the onboarding call with Trevor, and you can start whenever you want' — but the prospect deferred to think, so no payment, onboarding booking, agreement signature or welcome-email walkthrough was attempted. Note this is N/A because the call did not get there, not because the rep closed and skipped steps.

objection_plays.detail: 'let me think, and I can have some time to think about that, right?' at 00:43:58. None of the OA moves ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through can get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'. The rep replied 'Let me know what are your thoughts' and booked a callback.

Money was the live blocker — 'that would be a significant investment for me' and 'a substantial portion of my annual income'. The rep did run the isolate move: 'So apart from finances, like, sounds good to you, like there's nothing else?' and got a clean yes. Nothing after that ran: no 'you're not in a should-I place, you're in a how place', no offer to break payments up, no permission question for an honest financial conversation, and none of the six financial-picture questions — cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards, available credit, used vs available, or investments. The rep pivoted to scheduling instead.

Script gap — the prospect wanted a shorter engagement than the programme sells ('I don't envision me needing it for like, you know, multiple years because I'm not trying to get in shape'). There is no scripted play for a duration objection, so the rep improvised an off-menu three-month tier at $4,000 and steered him off the standard packages. That is a gap in the script, and it produced a pricing deviation.

Script gap — the prospect is a highly capable self-programmer who argued that method does not matter and consistency does ('it's not like the kettlebell's a magical tool, right'), and he had already used Trevor's free guide and found it beneath his level. There is no scripted play for a competent do-it-yourself substitute. The rep conceded the frame ('you're not our typical client because you're way ahead') rather than reframing to what coaching adds.

notes: Discovery collapsed into a comfortable conversation: the prospect talked at length, the rep asked few of the scripted questions, and phases 4, 5 and 6 never ran at all — so the offer landed with no pain, no consequence and no commitment behind it. The coachable moment is the money objection: the rep executed the isolate correctly and got a clean 'apart from the finances, everything else is good', then abandoned the play instead of exploring how to make it work, and discounted the product's duration rather than its value.
